subcategory: fort worth prairie limestone bench endemic

planting.note: Set out nursery-grown rosette divisions in early-to-mid spring once the ground has warmed, choosing a lean, rocky or calcareous site with sharp drainage.

directions: Plant in full sun on shallow, stony, calcareous soil that mimics the exposed limestone benches of the Fort Worth Prairie, where this narrow Texas endemic grows in small colonies. It needs essentially no irrigation once established and resents heavy or poorly drained ground, which quickly rots the crown. Slow-spreading rosettes gradually form clumps and send up a tall flower spike studded with white bell-shaped blooms in late spring, after which the plant is best left undisturbed for years. Division of offsets is the most reliable propagation method for gardeners, since seed-grown plants take many seasons to reach flowering size.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online
